question.text: A particle moving in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>xy</mi></math>-plane experiences a velocity dependent force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">υ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></msub><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">υ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></msub><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">υ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">υ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></msub></math> are the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></math> components of its velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">υ</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is the acceleration of the particle, then which of the following statements is true for the particle ?

options.text: kinetic energy of particle is constant in time
